summary: Optional top-level label of the run, printed at start-up with -v.

keys.meaning: Free-text description of the simulation.
keys.notes: Top-level key, not inside a block.

summary: Required block: input mesh, flow routing, boundary conditions, initial fields and advection scheme.

keys.unit: file ([file, v, c, z]; npz without extension)
keys.meaning: Input mesh: npz file name (without .npz) followed by the keys of the vertex coordinates (m, (n,3)), the triangle cells ((m,3) int) and the elevation (m) at each vertex.
keys.resolution: The mesh spacing sets the resolution of every process; no vertex may have more than 12 neighbours.
keys.notes: Raises if the key or the file is missing. Coordinates in m (Cartesian x, y, z; z = 0 on a flat mesh, on the sphere of radius `radius` for a global mesh).

keys.meaning: Maximum number of downslope receivers of the multiple-flow-direction routing (1 = single flow direction).
keys.range: 1 (single flow direction) up to the vertex degree (multiple flow direction); examples use 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; higher values spread the flow on hillslopes and flats
keys.resolution: With MFD the hillslope flow accumulation scales with the cell size (spread over neighbours), so the erosion of non-channel cells changes slightly with resolution.
keys.notes: Code default is 8 while the user guide says 1 to 6; the Fortran neighbour tables allow up to 12. Doc/code mismatch worth fixing. The partition exponent is fixed at 1.1 (a `flowexp` key is commented out in the parser and not read).

keys.meaning: Boundary condition of each edge of a flat mesh: o open (deep outlet), f fixed (outlet at edge elevation), w wall (no flux), c cyclic (needs a cylinder mesh, paired, serial only). Legacy 0/1 read as o/f.
keys.notes: Ignored on global meshes. Cyclic edges must come as an opposite pair, at most one pair, and only on one MPI rank. A fully walled domain does not conserve sediment over many steps.

keys.meaning: Run without surface processes (checks the inputs and forcing only).
Perform marine deposition of the sediment reaching the sea.
keys.notes: Must be True for marine deposition of the river load.

keys.meaning: Skip all sediment routing and deposition (continental and marine): eroded material leaves the model.
keys.notes: Undocumented in the user guide.

keys.meaning: Number of ghost-cell layers of the DMPlex partition (PETSc distribute overlap).
keys.notes: Undocumented expert key; the kernels assume one layer.

keys.meaning: Initial cumulative erosion/deposition field (m, positive = deposition) for every mesh vertex.
keys.resolution: Must be on the same mesh as npdata.
keys.notes: The key inside the file is fixed: `ed`.

keys.meaning: Initial stratigraphic layers: strataH (m), strataZ (m), phiS (-), each (mesh points, layers); optional stratK (-, erodibility multiplier), strataHf (m, fine thickness) and phiF (-) under dual lithology.
keys.resolution: Must be on the same mesh as npdata.
keys.notes: Needs a positive time: strat to be used; layers deepest first.

keys.meaning: Scheme for the horizontal advection of the surface and the stratigraphy by tectonics: hdisp.
keys.range: iioe2 for regional Eulerian runs; interp for plate motion on global meshes
keys.resolution: Eulerian schemes (upwind, iioe1, iioe2) diffuse fields over a few cells per event and do not carry the drainage across a lateral motion; interp is exact up to the interpolation.
keys.notes: Raises on any other value.

keys.default: none (one remap at the end of each event)
keys.meaning: With advect: interp, apply each tectonic event in remaps of about this many mesh spacings (barycentric weights).
keys.range: 0.5 to 2 (1 recommended when the motion should carry the drainage); 0.1-cell remaps smooth the valleys away
keys.resolution: Expressed in mesh spacings, so the remap distance scales with the cell size; the interval is a whole number of steps set by the fastest node, so with fast plates and long dt each remap can move more than requested.
keys.notes: Must be > 0 and only with advect: interp.

keys.meaning: Planet radius used for the spherical mesh geometry.
keys.notes: Global meshes only.

keys.meaning: Surface gravity used by the flexural isostasy.

summary: Required block: simulation period, time step, output and stratigraphic intervals, restart.

keys.meaning: Model start time.
keys.range: any (often negative for the past, e.g. -2e7)
keys.notes: end must be > start.

keys.meaning: Model end time.
Internal time step of the outer (explicit-in-time) process loop; inner solves are implicit.
keys.range: 1e2 to 1e5 yr in practice: 0.1 to 1 kyr for local glacial runs, 1 to 10 kyr regional, 1e4 to 2.5e5 yr global (examples 500 yr to 100 kyr); longer steps smooth transients and lag the coupling between processes
keys.resolution: Implicit solves stay stable at any dt, but accuracy is not: the marine picardSub should grow as dt/dx^2 grows, glacial abrasion needs Kg*|u_b|^l*dt well below the relief (see ice), and the remap interval of interp_remap is a whole number of steps.
keys.notes: Reset to tout if larger than tout.

keys.meaning: Output interval.
keys.range: a multiple of dt; 10 to 200 outputs per run is typical
keys.notes: Reduced to end - start if longer; increased to dt if shorter.

keys.meaning: Restart from this output step of a previous run in the same output dir.
keys.notes: Forces output: makedir to False.

keys.meaning: Interval at which a new stratigraphic layer is recorded.
keys.range: 1 to 10 dt; tout must be a multiple of it
keys.resolution: Layer thickness resolution is set by strat and the deposition rate, not by the mesh.
keys.notes: Required (> 0) for strata: dual, provenance and soil mode: regolith. Raises if tout is not divisible by strat.

summary: Output folder and options.

keys.meaning: Output directory name.
False: overwrite an existing folder of that name; True: create dir_N with a new number instead.
keys.notes: Set to False on restart.

keys.meaning: Enable the wall-clock phase profiler (also -p on the command line).
keys.notes: Undocumented in the user guide.

keys.meaning: HDF5 output compression: gzip (default level), a gzip level, or none for uncompressed (faster I/O, larger files).
keys.range: gzip; none on fast parallel file systems when I/O dominates
keys.notes: Undocumented in the user guide.

summary: Stream power law river incision and continental deposition (E = K P^d (P A)^m S^n).

keys.default: required (1e-12 when the block is absent)
keys.meaning: Erodibility coefficient of the stream power law E = K P^d (P A)^m S^n, with P A the discharge (m3/yr).
keys.range: With m = 0.5, n = 1 and d = 0: about 1e-7 to 1e-5 (examples 1e-6 to 5.5e-6 regional/global, 4e-5 on the uplifted-block test); strongly lithology and climate dependent, calibrate
keys.resolution: Keep K when changing the mesh: channel erosion at given area and slope is mesh independent, but MFD hillslope cells collect flow in proportion to their size, so the same K erodes them less on finer meshes (about 0.5^m per halving) and total yields can change; match first-step marine supply between meshes if needed.
keys.notes: Required inside spl.

keys.meaning: Exponent of the local precipitation in the erodibility, K P^d (Murphy et al. 2016).
keys.notes: Changes the units of K.

keys.meaning: Discharge exponent.
keys.resolution: none (but sets how K units and hillslope sensitivity scale)

keys.meaning: Slope exponent; n != 1 uses the non-linear SNES solver.
keys.notes: Non-linear runs (n != 1) are much more expensive.

keys.meaning: Continental deposition coefficient (Yuan et al. 2019): the fraction of the incoming load deposited in a cell is G * area / discharge = G / P (capped at 0.99). 0 = detachment limited.
keys.range: 0 to about rain/2 (in m/yr); examples 0 to 3
keys.resolution: Independent of the mesh spacing (the deposited thickness G Q dt / (P A) has no area left).
keys.notes: Keep G <= about half the rainfall rate: at the 0.99 cap the coupled solve becomes near singular (slow, spikes).

keys.meaning: Maximum non-linear iterations of the SPL SNES (n != 1 only).
Relative tolerance of the non-linear SPL solve (n != 1).
Absolute tolerance of the non-linear SPL solve (n != 1), on the elevation residual.
keys.notes: Unit inferred from the residual (elevation).

keys.meaning: Primary non-linear solver (n != 1); the other is the automatic fallback.
Preconditioner of the non-linear SPL Krylov solve (n != 1).
keys.range: hypre; gamg, bjacobi or asm as alternatives

summary: Hillslope creep (land and sea), marine and lake non-linear diffusion of fresh deposits, clinoform geometry and channel masking.

keys.default: required inside the block (0 when absent)
keys.meaning: Linear (or non-linear base) hillslope diffusivity on land.
keys.range: 1e-3 to 1e-2 m2/yr measured at the hillslope scale; effective values of 0.01 to 1 used on km meshes (examples 0 to 1)
keys.resolution: Diffusion also acts on one-cell-wide channels, so without channelQ the steady channel steepness grows on finer meshes (30.5, 41.6, 66.4 at 200, 100, 50 m with 0.2 m2/yr instead of 25); smoothing per step scales as D dt/dx^2. Set channelQ or choose the value for the mesh.

keys.default: required inside the block (0 when absent)
keys.meaning: Linear diffusivity of the seafloor (and lake floor) creep.
keys.range: 0 to a few m2/yr (examples 0 to 2); calibrate
keys.resolution: Smoothing per step scales as D dt/dx^2.

keys.meaning: Slope exponent of the non-critical non-linear creep law (Wang et al. 2024); 1 = linear.
keys.resolution: Gradients are lower on coarse meshes, so the non-linear term weakens with cell size.
keys.notes: Uses hillslopeKa/Km as coefficients. Results changed in Nov 2026 (flux, not its derivative).

keys.meaning: Critical slope of the Roering et al. (1999) non-linear creep law.
keys.resolution: Resolved slopes fall on coarser meshes, so fewer cells approach Sc there.
keys.notes: S/Sc capped at 0.8 internally.

keys.meaning: Number of terms of the truncated Taylor series of the critical-slope law (Barnhart et al. 2019); 0 = full Roering law.
keys.notes: Only with hillslopeSc > 0.

keys.meaning: Depth below sea level under which the marine depression filling and flow-direction smoothing are not applied.
keys.range: well below sea level, e.g. -1000 to -6000 m on flat models; leave the default on global models
keys.notes: Cut-off elevation is sea level + oFill; a value above sea level traps sediment at the coast.

keys.meaning: Transport coefficient of the non-linear (deposit-thickness dependent) marine and lake diffusion of fresh river deposits.
keys.resolution: A physical diffusivity: keep it when changing the mesh, but raise picardSub as about (dx_old/dx_new)^2.
keys.notes: fine_diff_factor of the strata block multiplies it for fine sediment.

keys.meaning: Slope of the clinoform top surface below sea level that caps the marine deposition height with distance from the coast.
keys.resolution: A gradient: on coarse meshes the coastal distance is coarser, but the cap is resolution independent.
keys.notes: Clamped to >= 1e-6.

keys.meaning: Maximum number of internal time steps of the adaptive marine TS solver per goSPL step.
keys.notes: Only with marineSolver: ts.

keys.meaning: Marine deposition coefficient (fraction of the incoming marine flux deposited per cell, capped at 0.99) of the coupled marine deposition solve.
keys.notes: Only active on global (spherical) models; ignored on flat meshes. The user guide does not say this.

keys.meaning: Distance from the coast beyond which the clinoform-distance cap and the marine fill are not applied (global models).
keys.notes: Used only on global meshes (coastDist).

keys.meaning: Volume above which a partially filled depression uses the bathymetric pile plus inlet bias geometry (together with nlPitDepth).
Depth above which a partially filled depression uses the diffusion path (both thresholds must be exceeded).
Non-linear diffusion coefficient used inside selected lakes/pits.

keys.default: 0.10 (0.50 when the diffusion block is absent)
keys.meaning: Fraction of each pit deposit concentrated at its inlets (delta seed); the rest fills from the bottom.
keys.notes: Clamped to [0, 1]. Code default differs with and without the block (0.10 vs 0.50). Different from strata: pitInletBias (per fraction, dual lithology).

keys.meaning: Marine and lake non-linear diffusion solver: lagged-diffusivity backward Euler (picard) or adaptive PETSc TS rosw (ts).
keys.notes: Unknown values fall back to picard. ts falls back to picard if it fails.

keys.meaning: Number of sub-steps of the picard marine solver per goSPL step.
keys.range: 10 to 100 (20 gave 1.4 % rms of ts on a 190k-node margin)
keys.resolution: Scale by about (dx_old/dx_new)^2 when refining (4x per halving) and with longer dt, since the sub-step diffusion number grows as dt/dx^2.
keys.notes: Minimum 1.

keys.meaning: Picard (lagged diffusivity) updates per sub-step.
keys.notes: Minimum 1.

keys.meaning: Discharge above which a land cell is a channel: held fixed by the hillslope diffusion, with the hillslope supply added to the same step's river load.
keys.range: channel-head area times rainfall: 1e4 to 1e6 m2 times P (e.g. 1e6 for 1 km2 at 1 m/yr); example 1e6
keys.resolution: Keep the channel-head area at least about 10 cell areas on the coarsest mesh used (A_c >= 10 dx^2); then the same value gives the same channels on every mesh. Avoid exact multiples of cell area times rain on regular meshes (ties).
keys.notes: Must be > 0. Recommended whenever hillslopeKa is not negligible.

summary: Diagnostic glacial model: ELA mass balance routed into an ice discharge, Bahr thickness, Glen sliding, abrasion, till and meltwater.

keys.meaning: Glacier terminus elevation; no ice below max(hterm, sea level).
keys.notes: Scalar or per-vertex map; also in glaciers[] events and the evol file (column 2).

keys.meaning: Equilibrium-line altitude: ablation below, accumulation above.
keys.range: near sea level (polar) to 5000-6000 m (tropics); example 1500 m
keys.notes: Per-vertex map recommended on global meshes.

keys.meaning: Ice-cap altitude: full precipitation captured as ice above it.
keys.range: a few hundred m above hela (example 1800 with hela 1500)
keys.notes: Must stay above hela everywhere.

keys.unit: file (csv: time yr, hterm m, hela m, hice m)
keys.meaning: Time series of the glacier geometry, interpolated linearly in time.
keys.notes: Takes precedence over maps and glaciers (the maps are then ignored).

keys.meaning: Number of MFD directions used to route the ice accumulation.
keys.resolution: More directions spread the ice over wider troughs on fine meshes.

keys.meaning: Weight of the below-ELA ablation in the net balance routed into the discharge (0 accumulation only, 1 true net, > 1 shorter tongues).
keys.notes: Only controls ice extent; till melt-out and meltwater use the raw ablation.

keys.meaning: Bahr width factor in H = eheight * fwidth * Q^0.3.
keys.notes: Only the product with eheight matters.

keys.meaning: Bahr thickness factor in H = eheight * fwidth * Q^0.3 (Q ice discharge, m3/yr).
keys.range: product eheight*fwidth chosen so that iceH is 1e1 to 1e3 m (example 0.5)
keys.notes: Unit of the product inferred from the formula; not stated in the docs.

keys.meaning: Basal sliding coefficient of the Glen/Budd sliding law u_b = A_s H^(n-1) |grad s|^(n-1) grad s.
keys.range: tune so that iceUb is tens of m/yr in temperate valley glaciers (example 0.3)
keys.notes: Unit inferred from the law (absorbs (rho_i g)^(n-1)).

keys.meaning: Glen sliding exponent n.
Discharge-conserving meltwater: the accumulated ice water is released where the ice melts out.
Fraction of precipitation converted to ice above the ELA.
Cap on the accumulation rate.
keys.notes: Set it for high-precipitation runs.

keys.meaning: Time series of {start, hela, hice, hterm} events (each uniform or [file, key]).
keys.notes: See ice.glaciers[].

summary: Time-stepped glacier geometry events (like climate events).

keys.meaning: Start time of the event (holds until the next).
ELA for this interval.
Ice-cap altitude for this interval.
Terminus elevation for this interval.

summary: Velocity-based glacial erosion E_g = Kg |u_b|^l and lateral wall erosion.

keys.meaning: Vertical abrasion coefficient.
keys.range: 1e-5 to 1e-4 with l = 1 (Humphrey and Raymond 1994 about 1e-4; example 3e-5)
keys.resolution: Stability: the abrasion per step Kg |u_b|^l dt must stay small against the relief (Kg = 3e-5 stable, 1e-4 unstable with dt = 5 kyr in the example); reduce Kg with longer dt.
keys.notes: Unit inferred (E in m/yr, u_b in m/yr): dimensionless for l = 1.

keys.meaning: Sliding-velocity exponent of the abrasion.
Lateral (valley-wall) erosion coefficient; widens troughs towards a U shape.
keys.notes: Kl >> Kg gives runaway widening.

keys.meaning: Velocity exponent of the lateral erosion.

summary: Glacial till transport and moraine deposition.

keys.meaning: Carry abraded rock as till and deposit it as moraine (False: send it to the rivers).
keys.notes: Inert while Kg = 0.

keys.meaning: Route the till down the ice-surface network to each terminus (False: spread the global volume over the ablation zone).

summary: Soil production, soil-aware SPL (SPACE-like) and soil transport.

keys.meaning: Erodibility of the soil (kappa_s); bedrock uses spl: K.
keys.range: a few times spl K (examples 1.6e-6 to 8e-6)

keys.unit: m/yr (without tempMap); m of soil per m of rain, - (with tempMap)
keys.meaning: Maximum soil production rate P0 in the exponential law P0 exp(-H/Hs).
keys.range: 1e-5 to 3e-4 m/yr (10 to 300 m/Myr; examples 3e-5 to 5e-5)
keys.notes: With tempMap the production is maxProd times the local rainfall times the Arrhenius factor (Norton et al. 2013, Eq. 8), so maxProd is then a production per metre of rain.

keys.meaning: Soil production decay depth Hs.
keys.notes: Must be positive.

keys.meaning: Roughness length H* weighting soil versus bedrock erosion (exp(-H/H*)).
Soil transport decay depth H0 of the soil diffusion (1 - exp(-H/H0)).
keys.notes: Diffusivities are hillslopeKa/Km.

keys.meaning: Fraction of P0 at which soil turns to bedrock; maximum soil thickness -ln(bedrockConv)*depthProd (0 = no cap).
Initial uniform soil thickness.
keys.notes: Ignored if soilMap is given.

keys.meaning: Initial soil thickness map (npz, one value per vertex).
Annual-mean surface temperature map enabling Arrhenius scaling of production.
keys.notes: Changes the meaning of maxProd (see above); also used by duricrust weather_Ea.

keys.meaning: Arrhenius activation energy of soil production.
keys.notes: Only with tempMap.

keys.meaning: Reference temperature at which production equals maxProd.
keys.notes: Only with tempMap.

keys.meaning: lumped: soil also absorbs deposits; regolith: soil is weathering regolith only, deposits go to the stratigraphy.
keys.notes: regolith needs time: strat > 0.

keys.meaning: Maximum iterations of the soil SNES.
Relative tolerance of the soil SNES.
Absolute tolerance of the soil SNES.
keys.notes: Unit inferred.

keys.meaning: Preconditioner of the soil SNES Krylov solve.
Primary soil non-linear solver; the other is the fallback.

summary: Time series of spatial multipliers of the erodibility K (surface lithology).

keys.meaning: Start time of the event (holds until the next).
keys.notes: Before the first event the factor is 1.

keys.meaning: Uniform erodibility factor.
keys.notes: One of uniform or map is required.

keys.meaning: Per-vertex erodibility factor map.

summary: Porosity-depth curve phi = phis exp(-z/z0s) of the (single-fraction or coarse) sediment.

keys.meaning: Surface porosity.
e-folding depth of the porosity.

summary: Dual lithology (coarse/fine) of the stratigraphy.

keys.meaning: Track coarse and fine sediment separately.
keys.notes: Needs time: strat > 0 (else forced off with a warning).

keys.meaning: Coarse fraction of the bedrock (composition of eroded bedrock).
Insert an infinite bedrock layer (bedrock_coarse_frac composition) beneath npstrata layers.
keys.notes: Only relevant with domain: npstrata.

keys.meaning: Multiplier of hillslopeKa/Km/nonlinKm for fine sediment (Cd = Cd*(fc + ff*factor)).
Porosity curve of the coarse fraction.
Porosity curve and erodibility factor of the fine fraction.
Per-fraction lake inlet bias; the contrast coarse - fine sets depth segregation.
keys.notes: Ignored if not a mapping.

summary: Coarse (sand) porosity curve.

keys.meaning: Surface porosity of coarse sediment.
Porosity e-folding depth of coarse sediment.

summary: Fine (silt/clay) porosity curve and erodibility.

keys.meaning: Surface porosity of fine sediment.
Porosity e-folding depth of fine sediment.
Fine erodibility relative to coarse (K_fine = K * k_factor).

summary: Per-fraction lake/pit deposition bias (dual lithology).

keys.meaning: Inlet bias of the coarse fraction.
keys.notes: Clamped to [0, 1].

keys.meaning: Inlet bias of the fine fraction.
keys.notes: Clamped to [0, 1].

summary: Passive source-rock class tracers carried through erosion, transport, deposition and stratigraphy.

keys.meaning: Number of source classes.
keys.notes: Needs time: strat > 0.

keys.meaning: Per-vertex source class map (values 0 to classes-1).
Single source class everywhere.

summary: Implicit Dupuit-Boussinesq water table, with optional duricrust and solute geochemistry.

keys.meaning: Saturated hydraulic conductivity K_h.
keys.notes: Scalar only in the code (float); the user guide claims a map or per-lithology value is possible, which is not the case.

keys.meaning: Drainable porosity S.

keys.unit: m (depth below surface), [file, key], or from_soil
keys.meaning: Depth of the impermeable base z_bed.
keys.notes: from_soil needs soil:.

keys.meaning: Permeable rock below the soil bedrock, only with aquifer_base: from_soil.
Floor of the saturated thickness.
Fraction of max(0, rain - evap) recharging the aquifer.
Return seepage to the rivers as baseflow.
Lake-aquifer volume coupling.
Fraction of glacial meltwater infiltrating under ice.
Infiltration multiplier for fine sediment (dual lithology).
Reference slope of the f/(1 + slope/ref) reduction.
Inner iterations of the unconfined non-linearity T(h).
Seepage free-boundary passes.
Generic duricrust.
Conservative solute geochemistry.

summary: Capillary-fringe induration that armors the erodibility.

keys.meaning: Formation rate k_form at full favourability and supply.
keys.notes: Not used when geochem: is on (precip_rate governs).

keys.meaning: Maximum crust thickness.
Centre of the capillary-fringe band on water-table depth.
Gaussian half-width of the band.
Restrict crust to groundwater discharge zones.
Exponent p on (rain - evap) in the proxy supply.
Arrhenius activation energy of the supply (uses soil tempMap).
Maximum fractional K reduction.
Also armor the hillslope diffusivity.
Crust removed per unit surface incision.
keys.notes: Unit inferred from the code.

keys.meaning: Slow disequilibrium decay away from the fringe.
Solute supply mode.

summary: Weathering supply Psi feeding crust formation.

keys.meaning: Climate proxy, explicit Maher-Chamberlain rate, or soil production.
keys.notes: rate/prodsoil fall back to proxy without soil.

keys.meaning: Equilibrium concentration (mode rate).
Damkohler-type weathering coefficient (mode rate).
keys.notes: Unit inferred from frac = 1 - exp(-Dw/(R L)).

keys.meaning: Flow path length L when soil is off (mode rate).
Relative weatherability (mode rate).
Listed in the user guide example but ignored by the parser here (only duricrust.weather_Ea is read).
keys.notes: Doc/code mismatch.

summary: Conservative multi-tracer solute geochemistry.

keys.meaning: Tracers.
Keep and report the closed solute budget.
Label for weatherability_by_class tables.
keys.notes: Needs provenance:.

keys.meaning: Standalone lithology label map.
Route the exported solute down the rivers.
Accumulate coastal delivery in a marine reservoir.
keys.notes: Needs river_load.

summary: One solute tracer.

keys.meaning: Tracer label.
Relative dissolution rate.
Per-class weatherability.
Fringe precipitation rate k_p.
keys.resolution: A rate: scale down with longer dt (near 1 saturates in one step at My dt).

keys.meaning: Crust volume per unit precipitated solute.

keys.unit: solute per m2 of cell area
keys.meaning: Dissolvable source-rock reservoir per unit cell area.
Saturation threshold (reserved, unused in the physics).
First-order in-transit loss along the river.
keys.resolution: Per receiver hop, so the loss per km grows on finer meshes.

summary: Eustatic sea level: a constant position and/or a curve through time.

keys.meaning: Sea-level elevation; when a curve is also given, it is added to every value of the curve (datum offset).
keys.range: 0 for present-day datum; examples -1000 to 0 m on meshes with a shifted datum
keys.notes: Shifts every sea-level dependent threshold (oFill is relative to it).

keys.unit: file (2 columns: time yr, sea level m; comma or whitespace separated, no header)
keys.meaning: Sea-level curve, interpolated linearly in time and held constant beyond its ends.
keys.range: eustatic amplitudes of tens of m (Milankovitch, up to about 120 m) to about 250 m (long-term Haq-type curves)
keys.resolution: Sea-level changes faster than dt are aliased: sample the curve at least at dt.

summary: List of rainfall (and optional evaporation) events, each holding from its start time until the next.

keys.meaning: Start time of the event.
keys.notes: Rain is 0 before the first event if it starts after time: start.

keys.meaning: Uniform rainfall rate.
keys.notes: Each event needs one of uniform, map or zscale.

keys.unit: [file, key] (m/yr; npz, one value per mesh vertex)
keys.meaning: Per-vertex rainfall map.
keys.notes: May point at the npdata file.

keys.meaning: Rainfall linear in the current elevation, P = A z + B, clamped at 0, re-evaluated every step.
keys.range: A of order 1e-4 to 1e-3 per yr (example 8e-4), B 0.1 to 1 m/yr
keys.notes: Cheap proxy without wind or rain shadow.

keys.meaning: Uniform evaporation rate subtracted from runoff and lake inflow.
keys.range: 0 to 2 m/yr (potential evaporation of arid regions up to about 2 to 3 m/yr)

keys.meaning: Per-vertex evaporation map.
Losing-stream mode: evaporation is debited from the accumulated discharge (global switch if any event sets it).
keys.notes: A few extra flow solves per step.

summary: Linear orographic precipitation (Smith and Barstad 2004) solved on the unstructured mesh; flat (2D) meshes only.

keys.meaning: Uniform wind speed.
keys.resolution: The advection length wind_speed x conv_time (or fall_time), 10 km with the defaults, should span several cells for the rain shadow to be resolved.
keys.notes: The orography block works on flat meshes only (refused on a sphere).

keys.unit: degrees (direction the wind comes from; 0 N, 90 E)
keys.meaning: Wind direction (meteorological convention).
Environmental lapse rate (with the two keys below sets Cw = ref_density * moist / env).
keys.notes: Must be non-zero.

keys.meaning: Moist adiabatic lapse rate.
Reference saturation water-vapour density.
keys.range: 1e-3 to 2e-2 kg/m3 (Cw bounds of the code docstring)

keys.meaning: Cloud water to hydrometeor conversion time tau_c.
Hydrometeor fallout time tau_f.
Uniform background (non-orographic) precipitation added everywhere.
keys.notes: Converted to m/yr with rainfall_frequency.

keys.meaning: Minimum precipitation floor (lee shadow).
Number of 1-hour storms per day used to convert mm/h into m/yr.

summary: List of tectonic events with vertical and/or horizontal displacement rates.

keys.meaning: Event start time.
Event end time.
keys.notes: An event with only start and end stops all motion for its duration.

keys.unit: [file, key] (m/yr; npz, one value per vertex)
keys.meaning: Vertical uplift (+) or subsidence (-) rate.
keys.notes: Applied at the start of each step.

keys.unit: [file, key] (m/yr; npz (n, 3) array vx, vy, vz)
keys.meaning: Horizontal (3D) displacement rates; z component 0 on flat meshes.
keys.range: 1e-3 to 1e-1 m/yr (1 to 100 mm/yr plate speeds)
keys.resolution: With Eulerian schemes the Courant number v dt/dx should stay below about 1; with interp see domain: interp_remap.
keys.notes: Needs domain: advect.

keys.meaning: Paleo-elevation map: cells at or below sea level are reset to it at each step of the event.
keys.notes: Undocumented in the user guide. Only used when the list has three elements (the third is not otherwise read).

summary: Flexural isostasy, D grad^4 w + drho g w = q with D = E Te^3 / (12 (1 - nu^2)).

keys.default: follows the mesh (fem flat, global sphere)
keys.meaning: fem: parallel finite-volume biharmonic on flat meshes; global: spherical-harmonic solve (rank 0) on global meshes.
keys.notes: A method set for the other kind of mesh stops at start-up with a message.

keys.meaning: Uniform effective elastic thickness Te (temap overrides it).
keys.range: 5e3 to 1e5 m (examples 5e3 to 3e4; oceanic and young lithosphere low, cratons high)
keys.resolution: The flexural parameter alpha = (4D/(drho g))^(1/4) is about 30 to 40 km for Te = 10 km and grows as Te^(3/4); the mesh spacing should be several times smaller than alpha.

keys.meaning: Density of the load (sediment/crust).
Asthenosphere (mantle) density.
Young's modulus E.
Poisson ratio.
North boundary condition (fem only).
keys.range: 0Slope0Shear or Mirror when loads are far from the edge
keys.resolution: Matters only when the flexural wavelength reaches the domain size.

keys.meaning: East boundary condition (fem only).
South boundary condition (fem only).
West boundary condition (fem only).
Apply flexure every interval steps, accumulating the load in between.
keys.resolution: Coarsens the loading history to interval x dt.
keys.notes: Minimum 1.

keys.meaning: Source points of the mesh to Driscoll-Healy grid interpolation (global only).
Resolution of the Driscoll-Healy grid (global only).
keys.range: 0.25 to 1 (coarser is cheaper with little change)
keys.resolution: Should be no coarser than the flexural wavelength (hundreds of km); finer than the mesh is wasted.

keys.meaning: Maximum Anderson/Picard iterations of the varying-Te global solve.
keys.notes: Unused without temap or with fem. Not the same key as spl: maxIter.

keys.meaning: Relative tolerance |dw|/|w| of the varying-Te iteration (global).
keys.notes: Minimum 1e-12.

keys.meaning: Under-relaxation of the varying-Te update (global).
keys.notes: Clamped to [1e-3, 1].

summary: Spatially and temporally variable elastic thickness events (fem and global).

keys.meaning: Event start time.
keys.notes: Start the first event at time: start: otherwise the parser inserts a row with Te 0 and no map, which _updateTe then tries to load as a map (looks like a crash path, unverified by a run).

keys.meaning: Uniform Te for this event.
keys.notes: A uniform 0 is allowed (Airy isostasy). Before the first event, the flexure block's thick is used. Works on flat and spherical meshes.

keys.unit: [file, key] (m; npz, one value per vertex)
keys.meaning: Per-vertex Te map.
